record.original_question: For multiplicative arithmetic functions f with property P, where f(p^alpha) depends only on alpha, every f-champion number lies in the set W of positive integers whose prime-exponent sequence is nonincreasing: if p and q divide N and p < q, then v_p(N) >= v_q(N). Since the counting function W(X) is therefore a universal upper bound for Q_f(X), can one find a smaller universal upper bound for Q_f(X) that is valid for every such f?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to find a smaller upper bound for Q f (X) which is valid for any f ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f: Z_{>0} → C be a multiplicative arithmetic function (i.e. f(1)=1 and f(mn)=f(m)f(n) whenever gcd(m,n)=1) with the property that the value f(p^α) at any prime power depends only on the exponent α, not on the prime p. For X ≥ 1, call a positive integer N ≤ X an f-champion (up to X) if |f(N)| ≥ |f(n)| for every positive integer n ≤ X, and let Q_f(X) denote the number of f-champions not exceeding X.

Let W be the set of positive integers N whose prime-exponent sequence is nonincreasing in the natural ordering of primes, i.e. for any primes p < q both dividing N one has v_p(N) ≥ v_q(N), where v_p(N) denotes the p-adic valuation of N. Let W(X) := #{N ∈ W : N ≤ X}.

It is known that, under the assumptions above, every f-champion belongs to W, and hence Q_f(X) ≤ W(X) for every X ≥ 1 and every f with the stated property.

Question: Does there exist a function B(X) with B(X) = o(W(X)) (or, more generally, B(X) ≤ W(X) for all large X and B(X) strictly smaller than W(X) in a quantitative sense) such that Q_f(X) ≤ B(X) holds for every X ≥ 1 and every multiplicative function f satisfying the hypothesis above? In other words, can the universal upper bound W(X) for Q_f(X) be improved?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for "f-champion numbers" and related terms did not return specific results addressing whether a universal upper bound smaller than W(X) for Q_f(X) is known. Related work on champion numbers (e.g., for the Dedekind Ψ function and similar extreme-value problems) exists, but no source confirming or refuting the existence of a smaller universal bound valid for all multiplicative f with the stated property was located. Status is unknown from accessible sources.

status_evidence.title: Extreme values of the Dedekind Ψ function
status_evidence.snippet: Studies champion numbers for the Dedekind Ψ function, illustrating the broader champion-number framework but not the universal Q_f(X) bound.
status_evidence.claim: Related champion-number analyses exist for specific multiplicative functions but do not address a universal bound smaller than W(X).
